brief.learner: Class 12 graduate in India; limited English; no AI background.
goals: Explain RAG in your own words.
Describe why external information helps an AI answer.
Trace preparation, retrieval, and generation in an example.
Identify why a RAG answer can still be wrong.

references.R1: https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/retrieval_augmented_generation — RAG pairs a generative model with retrieval; relevant information is supplied as context for an answer.
references.R2: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-how-it-works.html — A common preparation method splits documents into passages and indexes them for retrieval. Retrieved passages help answer a question. Updated documents must be prepared or synced before they are searchable; updates are not guaranteed to be instant (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-data-source-sync-ingest.html).
references.R3: https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/retrieval-augmented-generation/ — RAG uses external knowledge without requiring retraining for each document update. It can improve answers but does not guarantee correctness; source quality and retrieval matter. The model can generate wrong information even with accurate source material (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/reducing-hallucinations-in-llm-agents-with-a-verified-semantic-cache-using-amazon-bedrock-knowledge-bases/).

checkpoints.condition: Expand Retrieval-Augmented Generation and explain retrieval plus generation.
Explain why a model may need external or updated information.
Explain document preparation, relevant-passage retrieval, and generation using those passages.
Include one fictional example with a question, source passage, and supported answer.
Explain each essential technical term at first use.
Explain that retrieval can miss relevant material and generated answers can still be wrong.
Support core factual claims with reference IDs; contradict none of the supplied notes.
Include an exercise and a correct explanation that tests a learning goal.
Use beginner-friendly English without assumed AI knowledge, and explain concepts before depending on them in later sections.
